solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cure six-footer; to die otherwise

parts.note: an ant is an insect, and insects have six legs, so it is a six-footer

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters of to die are put in another order

explanation.surface: Desperate advice: cure the giant, or let it die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' sounds like a tall person, but it is an insect with six feet. 'otherwise' rearranges TO DIE into IDOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that counteracts a poison, so it is a cure.

clue.text: Demand on graduate from south somewhere in Scotland

indicators.note: in a down answer, read from the bottom up

explanation.surface: A graduate from the south makes demands in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From south' sounds like someone's origin; in a down clue it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: Online travel firm has little about rent and cover

indicators.note: the word for little goes about the word for rent, wrapping round it

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
a rip is a rent or tear
a visor is a cover or shield for the face or eyes

explanation.surface: A travel company with only a small sum for rent and insurance cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid for lodging, but here it is a tear. TAD goes 'about' RIP, then VISOR follows.
explanation.definitionFit: TripAdvisor is a well-known website of travel reviews and bookings, a company operating online.

clue.text: "Bash rodents eating bread" is command

indicators.note: the rodents take the bread inside

parts.note: a do or bash is a party
naan (also spelt nan) is Indian bread

explanation.surface: An order to hit the mice in the bread bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' reads as a verb, to hit; it is a noun, a party, which a DO also is.
explanation.definitionFit: Command in the sense of mastery or control is dominance.

clue.text: Liking head of nation to be brought down

indicators.note: the head of the word is its first letter, the one at the top of this down answer
in a down answer, bringing a letter down moves it lower in the word, here two places

explanation.surface: A wish to see a country's leader toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'head of' STATE is its S; it is 'to be brought down' below the next two letters, so STA becomes TAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste for something is a liking or preference for it.

clue.text: Duplicated recording containing single

indicators.note: the recording holds the other word inside it

parts.note: CD, a compact disc recording: first half

explanation.surface: A studio note: the tape was copied, and it has the single on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' reads as a pop record, fitting the recording; it is only the adjective, alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloned means copied exactly, duplicated.

clue.text: Girl from France, the content of mural

indicators.note: what is inside the word, without its ends

explanation.surface: A French girl painted in a wall picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places a French girl in a painting; 'from France, the' just asks for the French word for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: any girl's first name will do for 'girl', and this is a common one, as in Petrarch's beloved.

clue.text: Nothing to fasten bar back on camera

indicators.note: bar means except, so this letter is left out of the word for fasten
the back on the camera word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of camera is A

explanation.surface: No way to attach the rear bar to a camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a rod, but it means except: NAIL loses the letter at the 'back on' CAMERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is a score of zero, so it means nothing at all.

clue.text: Old-fashioned son bound by moral obligation

indicators.note: tied inside the other word

parts.note: s = son, as in family trees

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned son tied by duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a description of a dutiful son; the definition sits at the front, and 'bound by' puts the son inside the obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty can mean dull and old-fashioned, as in a dusty answer.

clue.text: Derision about irrational love for venomous type

indicators.note: the derision wraps round the rest

explanation.surface: Mocking someone's senseless passion for a poisonous character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational love' reads as one idea, a mad passion; it is two pieces, the irrational number pi and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: an arachnid with a stinging tail, so a creature of the poisonous kind.

clue.text: Recalled trap used in duplicate puzzles

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the whole build is read backwards
the trap is used in the duplicate word, placed inside it

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: A trap called back and reused in identical puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: GIN, an old word for a snare, goes 'used in' SAME to make SAMGINE, and 'Recalled' turns all of it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmas are mysteries or riddles, things that puzzle people.

clue.text: Items snapped up close

indicators.note: snapped like a twig, the letters of UP CLOSE are broken and reset

explanation.surface: Paparazzi snapping things close up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a photographer's close-up. 'Items' in the gossip-column sense are couples who are dating.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people seen together romantically are an item, so several such pairs are items: couples.

clue.text: Approached an errand drunkenly, having imbibed whiskey

indicators.note: a drunk's letters stagger into a new order
the whiskey goes into the mix

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone went out on a job after a few whiskies.
explanation.walkthrough: The whiskey sounds like the drink that caused the staggering; it is just the letter W, which joins the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, as a phrasal verb: came closer, both in the past tense.

clue.text: Cross whichever bridges lead to getting Romeo

indicators.note: the word for whichever bridges, spanning either side of, the other letters

parts.note: any means whichever, as in take any one

indicators.note: the lead to a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of getting is G
Romeo is R in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Crossing whichever bridge takes you to Romeo, as in a lovers' quest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the verb to go over a bridge, but it is the adjective. ANY 'bridges' G plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross is an informal word for annoyed, so it means angry.

clue.text: Composer's vault plagued with ghosts

indicators.note: troubled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A composer's tomb is haunted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer's' reads as possessive, whose vault; the 's is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the English writer of The Planets suite, one of many possible composers.

clue.text: Third character dropped from team of fantastic folk

indicators.note: the letter is dropped from the team word, left out of it

parts.note: a football or cricket team is an eleven
the third character of the team word is E

explanation.surface: A third player is left out of a team of fantasy creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: ELEVEN loses its 'Third character', the second E.
explanation.definitionFit: Elven is the adjective for elves, the magical beings of fairy tales and fantasy fiction.

clue.text: Enthusiasm when accepting relay with four going round

indicators.note: accepting means the word for when takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: going round means the pieces for relay and four are read backwards
with means the second piece is added alongside the first, so the two are joined in order

parts.note: send means relay, pass on a message
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Keenness shown as a relay team of four runs round the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relay' looks like a race but is the verb to pass on, and 'going round' turns the letters backwards rather than circling a track.
explanation.definitionFit: Avidness is eagerness or keenness, a strong appetite for something.

clue.text: Given a ship and one grand, returned home

indicators.note: sent back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a den is a home or lair

explanation.surface: Someone got a ship and a thousand pounds and came back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned home' reads as a sailor getting back; 'returned' only turns DEN round.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: allotted, as in 'given a task' or 'assigned a task'.

clue.text: Dash around in square gathering tree's first fruit

indicators.note: the built letters go in the square number, inside it

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three

indicators.note: around means turned round, so those letters are read backwards
the dash word is gathering the letter, taking it inside
first means the opening letter of the word for tree

parts.note: the first letter of tree is T

explanation.surface: Rushing round a town square to gather a tree's first fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: RACE 'gathering' T makes RATCE; 'around' turns it to ECTAR, which goes 'in' NINE. 'square' is the number nine, not a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a stone fruit.

clue.text: Steady sea ferries advanced fast

indicators.note: the sea carries the other letters inside it

parts.note: MED, the Mediterranean Sea: first two letters
a = advanced, as in A level
fast and sure both mean firm, secure

explanation.surface: A calm sea carries a speeding ship forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as quick; here it means fixed or firm, as in hold fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a pace that is even and deliberate, unhurried and regular.

clue.text: Introduces American woman with vice

explanation.surface: Someone introducing a wicked American woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase, so the answer is the two-word phrasal verb; 'with' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher in is to introduce or bring in.

clue.text: Crow and rook tucked into baked product

indicators.note: the rook goes inside the product

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: Two birds eating something baked.
explanation.walkthrough: The rook looks like the second bird; it is the chess piece. Crake is a dialect word for a crow.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern English dialect a crake is a crow or raven.

clue.text: Game board art student covers

indicators.note: the words wrap round the answer

explanation.surface: A board game from an art student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game board' runs together as a board game; the break comes after 'Game', and the board is darts' own.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub game of throwing darts at a board.

clue.text: Daughter finished port

explanation.surface: A daughter has finished her port.
explanation.walkthrough: Port sounds like the drink the daughter finished; it is a harbour town. Dover is the English Channel ferry port.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is a port on the south-east coast of England.

clue.text: Be silent and mimic model

explanation.surface: Advice to a quiet copycat model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a noun, a fashion model; it is the verb, to form or shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: a sculptor who models clay forms it.

clue.text: Try essentially dull remains after burning stews

parts.note: have a go = have a try

indicators.note: the essence, the core letters, of the word

parts.note: ashes are what is left after a fire

explanation.surface: A burnt stew with dull leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the far end, and 'burning' makes it look like a kitchen failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Goulash is a Hungarian meat stew.

clue.text: Not disheartened wearing uniform that is free

indicators.note: the word is worn inside the others

parts.note: Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
NOT without its middle letter, O

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful in uniform, and so free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not disheartened' reads as cheerful; it is the word NOT losing its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: undoing a knot or rope frees whatever it held.

clue.text: Veteran against eating bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters of eating go wild

explanation.surface: An old soldier who refuses to eat bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' looks like a container signal, but it is the anagram fodder: 'bananas' rearranges it to INTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintage car is a veteran one, old and of a classic period.

clue.text: Fan that's attached to bolt

definitions.meaning: an enthusiast, a devotee: first sense
the threaded fastener screwed on to a bolt: second sense

explanation.surface: An admirer who never leaves someone's side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' tempts as running away; it is the threaded rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is both a fan and the part that fastens on a bolt.

clue.text: One turning writerly almost finished novel

indicators.note: a word that is almost finished stops one letter short of its end
new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A writer nearly done with a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' and 'writerly' make a book; 'novel' is the rearranging signal, not the book.
explanation.definitionFit: A twirler is someone who twirls, one turning round.

clue.text: Fairly despicable person snubbed present

parts.note: a rat is a despicable person
HERE = present, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A nasty person snubbed a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is HERE, present in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as adverbs of degree: 'fairly cold' and 'rather cold' both mean somewhat cold.

clue.text: Fault editor that's gone to the opposition?

explanation.surface: An editor at fault who has joined a rival paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: the editor who defected went over to the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: To defect is to desert to the opposing side.
